note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure.
  - New severe constant headache x 3 days; no clear trigger/exposure identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression.
  - Sudden onset upon awakening 3 days ago; continuous since.
  - Severity 8/10 at worst; improves to ~5/10 with ibuprofen but does not resolve.
  - Diffuse pain with right supraorbital predominance; photophobia; intermittent “shooting lights”/visual disturbance; mild nausea without vomiting.
  - Able to sleep; not waking from sleep; present on awakening.
  - Brief stabbing pain when standing quickly; sensation of “something moving” with abrupt head movements. Not clearly worse with cough/valsalva.
  - No fever, no URI symptoms.
- ENT symptoms (as applicable): throat swelling/closure sensation (not reported), voice change (not reported), dysphagia/odynophagia (not reported), drooling (not reported), nasal/ocular symptoms (photophobia and positive visual phenomena; denies nasal/sinus symptoms), stridor/noisy breathing (not reported), dyspnea (not reported), swelling (lips/tongue/uvula/face not reported), ear/neck symptoms (denies sore ears; no neck pain reported).
- Relevant past episodes and treatments (including any prior hospital care or injection therapy).
  - Prior headaches mild and intermittent; typically <2 days and responsive to ibuprofen.
  - No prior severe headaches; no ED visits; no injection therapies.
- Allergies and current medications (mark missing dose/route/frequency as “not documented”).
  - Allergies: No known drug allergies.
  - Medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill (name not documented; started ~1 year ago); ibuprofen PRN for headache (dose/route/frequency not documented). Paracetamol/acetaminophen recommended to use with prescribed NSAID alternative (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Any relevant social context (e.g., accompaniment/supervision).
  - Lives alone; works from home; missed/limited work due to headache. Non-smoker; alcohol ~3 drinks once weekly; no recreational drugs. Recent eye exam reportedly normal. No recent travel. Family history: mother with severe migraines.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution (e.g., lips, tongue, uvula, face) if stated.
  - None reported.
- Airway/breathing descriptors if stated (e.g., stridor, work of breathing).
  - No stridor or respiratory distress reported.
- Mental status and associated features (e.g., dizziness, syncope) if stated.
  - Alert and conversant. Mild nausea; no vomiting; no focal neurologic symptoms reported.
- Vitals and examination findings only if mentioned; otherwise write “Not recorded.”
  - Not recorded.
- Presence of another person with the patient (if stated).
  - Patient is alone.

Assessment:
- Concise working clinical impression.
  - New, severe persistent headache with photophobia and visual phenomena—suspected migraine with aura; secondary causes considered given estrogen-containing OCP use. ENT sinus pathology unlikely.
- Brief evidence summary derived from the transcript.
  - Sudden onset on awakening; constant for 3 days; right supraorbital emphasis; photophobia and visual “shooting lights”; mild nausea; partial NSAID response; afebrile; no sinus/URI symptoms; normal recent optometry; on combined OCP; family history of migraine; no focal neurologic deficits by history.
- Reference the DDx succinctly:
  - Migraine with aura (possible status migrainosus) — High likelihood: visual phenomena and photophobia with moderate–severe pain and family history; persistent >72 hours. Opposing: first significant episode; continuous course.
  - Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) — Medium likelihood: estrogen OCP risk with new persistent severe headache and visual symptoms; some positional sensitivity. Opposing: no focal deficits, seizures, or papilledema reported.
  - Tension-type headache — Low–Medium likelihood: constant diffuse pain; able to sleep. Opposing: photophobia/visual aura and severity less typical.
- No conflict noted between transcript and DDx.

Plan:
- Immediate actions taken/advised.
  - Arrange in-person evaluation for full neurologic examination and fundoscopic assessment; check blood pressure.
  - Prescribe NSAID alternative to ibuprofen and use with paracetamol/acetaminophen as advised; take with food.
  - Continue current combined OCP for now; re-evaluate contraceptive choice if migraine with aura is confirmed (may require change).
- Specific patient/caregiver instructions.
  - If symptoms improve and resolve before the appointment, contact clinic to reassess need for in-person review.
- Escalation criteria/red flags.
  - Seek urgent care/ED if headache becomes unbearable or rapidly worsening, changes character, or if any red flags occur: new neurological deficits (weakness, numbness, speech/vision loss), severe or persistent vomiting, confusion, fever, neck stiffness, syncope, or seizures.
- Follow-up.
  - Book support team appointment for examination and BP check; consider neurology referral based on findings and persistence/severity.
  - Discuss migraine management strategies and contraceptive options at review if aura confirmed.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements.
  - Vitals (including BP) and temperature; complete neurologic exam; fundoscopic findings.
  - Exact medication names and doses (NSAID prescribed, OCP brand), dosing schedules.
  - Detailed aura description (type, duration, evolution), precipitating factors/triggers, caffeine and sleep history, hydration.
  - Thrombosis risk assessment (personal/family history, recent immobilization/dehydration), pregnancy status.
  - ENT exam (sinus tenderness, nasal endoscopy if indicated).
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx.
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality.
  - Minor audio issues and redactions; overall content understandable; no physical exam recorded.
